requisitions.externalDescription: SUMMARY The Parts Runner is responsible for the pick-up and delivery of parts, supplies, and vehicles for Fleet Services, also cleaning and re-stock the parts room and fuel island. This is an hourly position that will work a maximum of 29 hours/week. ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES The following duties and responsibilities are illustrative of the primary function of this position and are not intended to be all inclusive. Drives vehicle to transport parts and supplies to and from a variety of locations. Re-stock and cleans the Parts Room. Assists the Shop Operations with vehicle shuttle and shop clean-up. Cleans and performs daily checks on delivery vehicle. Answers phones and provides general information as needed. Stocks and cleans fuel island. SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES This position is not responsible for the supervision of regular City employees.

Job Summary Instruct and lead a variety of classes, hikes, rock climbing, outdoor skills, natural resource education and/or snowshoeing/cross country ski trips for the Recreation Division. Working knowledge of trip leading, outdoor safety, Colorado ecosystems, layering principles, outdoor skills, ecology, wildlife management, and instruction necessary. Work Schedule: This is a part-time, fluctuating hourly position that plans for and teaches classes year-round. Program hours vary depending on instructor schedule. Evening and weekend availability required. Essential job functions: The following duties and responsibilities are illustrative of the primary functions of this position and are not intended to be all inclusive. - Assist with the coordination of trips including but not limited to phone calls and emails to book venues, research information for potential trips, and contact participants on trip reminders, updates or cancellations. - Demonstrate competency in teaching and monitoring physical activity. - Practice good personal health and fitness habits. - Check physical environments, trail conditions, and weather for safety hazards before class/activity begins. - Inform supervisor of any safety concerns regarding trails, equipment, or participants. - Safely drive program participants to and from trailhead locations and destinations, following all City of Fort Collins driver policies. - Inform supervisor of conditions and needs of program supplies. - If the instructor is unable to guide, it is her/his responsibility to find a substitute. - Fill out all appropriate payroll documentation. - Attend an Employee and Volunteer Orientation and trainings. - Attend annual safety meeting. Supervisory responsibilities: This person could supervise volunteers.

Summary: Under administrative supervision of the fitness coordinator, this position is to instruct group fitness classes in one or more specific formats to recreation participants of various fitness levels and abilities. Must be able to perform essential duties and responsibilities in a manner consistent with the stated values of the City of Fort Collins and the Recreation department. Essential Duties and Responsibilities: The following duties and responsibilities are illustrative of the primary functions of this position and are not intended to be all inclusive. -Lead and instruct safe and effective group fitness classes in a welcoming, fun and motivating atmosphere. -Plan to teach a class that matches the title, description, and level of the specific class or classes. Responsible to demonstrate, supervise and assist participants in proper technique of various exercises and routines. To minimize injury and improve effectiveness, may need to correct participant techniques during class. -Explain and enforce safety rules and proper use of exercise equipment. -Instruct ongoing classes on scheduled days and times each week, as agreed upon and assigned by supervisor. -Show up on time to class, prepared to begin class on time. Must arrive to facility and clock in anywhere between 5-15 minutes before class time (instructor is considered tardy clocking in under 5 minutes before class). Instructor may be required to set-up equipment for class use. -Provide customer service to participants by consistently engaging with others, greeting them, welcoming new individuals, answering questions, or helping to find the answer, creating rapport and a fun group atmosphere. -Communicate to class participants with announcements including but not limited to reminders to sign up, sessions beginning/ending, class changes and/or additions, days with no class, other updates from facility, or supervisor. -Always conduct self in a professional manner in accordance with City of Fort Collins and Recreation policies and procedures. Required to wear a City of Fort Collins provided staff shirt when on duty, and follow dress and appearance polices. -End class on time according to the scheduled time. 50-55 minutes of class instruction time for an hour-long class. May be required to put equipment away at end of class. -Help keep fitness rooms, equipment, and storage closets clean and organized. Report areas of concern or needs to supervisor in a timely manner regarding equipment and rooms. -Responsible to find an appropriate substitute instructor for assigned classes when needed within a reasonable time frame. -Demonstrate teamwork and consistent communication by actively subbing for other instructors, reading weekly update emails from supervisor, passing along feedback received to supervisor, and attending all mandatory fitness staff meetings. -Maintain current certification(s) at instructors’ expense and keep current on trends and advancements in your training or specialization. Maintain an understanding and knowledge of exercise science, nutrition, and wellness within the scope of your certification and training. Supervisory Responsibilities: This position is not responsible for the supervision of employees.

The Wellness Program Intern will work with the Wellness Team to implement City-wide wellness programming. Interns will engage in needs assessments; program development and program implementation. Interns will assist with administrative roles associated with the development and implementation of our City-wide Wellness Program. Interns will also help maintain the internal Wellness website on SharePoint, Wellness e-newsletters, and various other communication tools. Interns may also assist with large wellness programs and projects such as health screenings, and the Well Days Incentive Program. Note to Applicants: This position is for the Spring semester, – Jan - June 2027 Location: Wellness Annex, 214 Howes St. 700 Wood St, Utilities Service Center Primary Activities: Assist with program marketing Plan and implement a multi-week incentive program Assist with planning and conducting large wellness events Work with City departments on their wellness needs. Maintain the Wellness website Conduct fitness room orientations and stretch sessions

Job Summary This second-level practitioner supports floodplain management and stormwater master planning by applying engineering principles and regulatory knowledge to a range of complex floodplain reviews, hydrologic and hydraulic modeling, and stormwater infrastructure planning. This position applies working knowledge and professional judgement to evaluate project compliance with applicable regulations and standards, adapt established procedures to varied situations, and guide technical decisions for stormwater master planning and other City-led projects. The position works under moderate supervision and in collaboration with development review staff, consultants, internal departments, and the public. Essential Duties and Responsibilities • Reviews development proposals, capital improvement projects and projects from other City departments for compliance with City Code, applicable state and federal floodplain regulations and sound engineering practices. • Serves as project manager or project team member for assigned stormwater master planning studies. Conducts and/or coordinates hydrologic, hydraulic, alternatives and selected-plan analyses to evaluate flood risk and infrastructure needs. • Develops, reviews and modifies one-dimensional and two-dimensional hydrologic and hydraulic models. • Develops preliminary and final cost estimates for proposed stormwater improvements. • Assists with the preparation and review of technical reports, specifications, plans, designs, schedules and other project deliverables. • Assists with the selection and management of engineering consultants and professional service providers; monitors assigned consultant work for scope, schedule, budget and quality. • Assists with the preparation and administration of project contract documents and reviews consultant and contractor invoices for assigned projects. • Evaluates stormwater quality considerations and incorporates applicable requirements into stormwater planning and improvement projects. • Coordinates assigned projects and technical reviews with development review staff and other City departments. • Participates in meetings with internal and external stakeholders to discuss technical issues, project requirements and potential solutions. • Prepares and reviews maps, exhibits, analyses and other technical information with geospatial mapping tools. • Maintains accurate project, floodplain and regulatory records and documentation. • Assists with the City's participation in the Community Rating System program, including three-year verification visits and annual activities. • Assists with emergency preparedness and response activities related to flooding, including serving as an on-call person for the City’s flood warning system for an estimated two weeks a year as part of a rotation. • Conducts public outreach related to flood awareness and safety, floodplain map adoptions and stormwater master plan adoptions. Prepares public outreach materials and presentations. Plans and attends outreach events. This job description is a living document and may not be all-inclusive; employees are responsible for other duties as assigned.

Job Summary Exciting opportunity for an experienced transportation demand management (TDM) professional to lead the City of Fort Collins TDM program branded as Shift Your Ride. This position serves as the sole program administrator for Shift Your Ride, responsible for day-to-day implementation, ride matching platform administration, and ongoing program facilitation, with consultant partnerships as needed for specific projects. The ideal candidate is an engaging, forward-thinking, and collaborative individual with a passion for sustainable transportation. Additionally, the person in this position should be a self-motivated individual who is comfortable taking the initiative to manage and advance the City's TDM program. Essential Duties and Responsibilities • Develops and builds on City relationships and partnerships with existing and new employers, developers, property management companies, schools and universities, hospitals, the visitor and tourism industry, and other institutions and organizations to develop sustainable commuting and trip reduction programs. • Develops and promotes policies incentivizing sustainable modes, including local and regional transit, e-scooter and bike share, ridesharing, vanpooling, electric vehicles, and teleworking. • Collaborates with the three program areas within FC moves - Mobility Management and Planning, Active Modes, and Education, Outreach, and Engagement to effectively integrate Transportation Demand Management related work. • Administers the Shift Your Ride ride-matching platform, including member management, challenges, quarterly incentives, and employer subnetworks. • Facilitates the residential and employer travel surveys. • Attends events to promote the Shift Your Ride Program and sustainable mobility options, which may include Bike to Work Day, Open Streets, and other related events. • Monitors legislation and policies related to TDM and provides input and recommendations as needed. • Lends expertise and advocates for the integration of TDM into plans, processes, policies, and programs, such as the City's development review and city code processes, and the Metropolitan Planning Organization (MPO) Transportation Improvement Program. • Pursues and manages grants. • Leads or supports the development and execution of communications and marketing materials, creative engagement campaigns, events, and initiatives promoting the Shift Your Ride Transportation Options Program and TDM strategies. • Support the City's Electric Vehicle Readiness Roadmap (EVRR) by promoting EV options and programs, such as a future EV Group Buy Program.

Job Summary This first-level supervisor leads a small team of customer service staff, applying knowledge of customer service principles, account and billing practices and the ordinances, policies and regulations that govern the service area. This position applies working knowledge and judgment to tasks of moderate complexity, making day-to-day decisions within established procedures to resolve customer issues and keep service operations running smoothly. The role supervises and trains staff and may perform the work of those supervised. It works under the direction of management and in collaboration with other departments and outside entities to deliver effective and efficient customer service. Essential Duties and Responsibilities • Supervises customer service staff and additional staff as assigned working in a designated service area such as a front counter, window or service desk. • Develops and administers training programs. • Resolves customer complaints, issues and problems. • Interprets City and department policies, procedures, codes and regulations for division personnel and customers. • Administers and monitors ongoing programs and routines and special projects for the department. • Initiates changes in working conditions and use of equipment to increase efficiency. • Responsible for financial or budget functions that may include developing and maintaining the department budget, purchasing equipment and supplies, accounts payable and receivable, payroll actions or timesheet processing. • Participates as part of the department’s management team. • Coordinates with other City departments and external entities. • May perform the functions of the employees supervised. • May act as staff liaison for the department. • May provide administrative support to managers and other technical staff as needed. • Performs word processing and data entry and may maintain databases and spreadsheets. This job description is a living document and may not be all-inclusive; employees are responsible for other duties as assigned.

Job Summary The Operator I, Transportation Operations (Asphalt) performs a variety of skilled and semi-skilled duties supporting the construction, maintenance, repair, and upkeep of asphalt streets, alleys, and related transportation infrastructure. The position operates and maintains heavy equipment such as dump trucks, skid steers, front-end loaders, backhoes, paving equipment, street sweepers, and other equipment used for asphalt preparation, placement, patching, repair, and roadway cleanup. Responsibilities include identifying and repairing deteriorated or eroded pavement, preparing work areas, removing roadway debris, assisting with asphalt paving and maintenance activities, and supporting traffic control and work-zone safety. The Operator I also performs routine equipment maintenance, records daily work activities, responds to emergency and after-hours roadway needs, and may assist with snow removal and other transportation operations as assigned. The position requires a strong commitment to safety, the ability to work outdoors and in varying conditions, operate a variety of heavy equipment, follow maps and work plans, perform basic computer data entry, and work effectively as part of a transportation operations team. Essential Duties and Responsibilities • Operates and maintains equipment which may include front-end loader, bulldozer, skid steer, dump truck, backhoe, farm tractors, pavement marking sign equipment, street sweeper, paving equipment, mowing or other vegetation management equipment, and other heavy equipment as needed. • Patch broken or eroded pavement; remove debris from roadway. • May construct and maintain pavement markings / signs, and signals and participate in traffic control activities. • Perform snow removal and operate snow removal equipment. • Input daily work data into a computer. • Perform general building maintenance. • May train and oversee other operators or hourly employees. • Shift work and emergency responses activities may be required. This job description is a living document and may not be all-inclusive. Employees are responsible for all other duties as assigned. Employees must be able to perform the essential duties of this job with or without a reasonable accommodation.

Job Summary This manager directs the engineering, reliability and security of the broadband network by applying advanced knowledge of network architecture, fiber-optic transport, data routing and cybersecurity principles. The position resolves complex and varied challenges, developing new approaches to capacity, resilience and technology lifecycle needs where established procedures do not exist. It makes operational decisions on network design, standards, staffing, vendor selection and budget within approved organizational strategy, and recommends longer-term investments to senior leadership. The position manages and develops engineering and technical support staff and works with minimal oversight in partnership with operations, sales, customer support and regulatory teams to deliver a scalable, secure and high-performing network. Essential Duties and Responsibilities • Provides strategic and operational leadership for network engineering, setting direction and priorities that ensure reliable, scalable and high-performing broadband service delivery. • Supervises, mentors and evaluates engineering and technical support staff, including hiring, assigning work, setting performance expectations, conducting reviews and recommending pay and personnel actions, to build technical expertise, accountability and continuous improvement. • Manages the division budget, staffing and resource plans, and oversees equipment lifecycle, inventory, technology standards and capital planning, forecasting current and future operational and capital needs. • Oversees the design, implementation, optimization and maintenance of broadband network infrastructure, including fiber-optic transport and data routing systems, ensuring redundancy, capacity and adoption of emerging technologies. • Leads network troubleshooting, incident response and root-cause analysis to minimize service disruptions and directs technical support operations to meet service-level objectives and resolve customer issues. • Develops and enforces network engineering standards, cybersecurity practices, disaster recovery plans and change management procedures, and establishes performance metrics, service-level objectives and escalation procedures to measure and sustain network health. • Manages the division budget, staffing and resource plans and oversees equipment lifecycle, inventory, technology standards and capital planning, forecasting current and future operational and capital needs. • Oversees vendor evaluation, contracting, onboarding and performance management for network equipment and technical services to ensure quality, cost control and contract compliance. • Leads initiatives that improve network efficiency, reliability, scalability and customer experience, and guides continuous improvement of technical support procedures, training and knowledge resources. • Coordinates with internal departments to ensure seamless service delivery, and supports strategic planning, regulatory compliance and broadband expansion. • Supports the development and management of intergovernmental agreements related to broadband services and shared network infrastructure. This job description is a living document and may not be all-inclusive; employees are responsible for other duties as assigned.

Job Summary This operations level Assistant Superintendent assists in planning, coordinating, supervising, and executing golf course maintenance operation applying specialized knowledge of turfgrass management, agronomy, irrigation, horticulture, and equipment. Directs and participates in the daily care of golf course grounds, performs complex and varied work requiring adaptation to changing weather, turf, course, environmental, staffing, and operational conditions. Exercises independent judgment within established policies, procedures, and direction from the Golf Course Superintendent. Provides direct supervision and leadership to seasonal and full-time maintenance staff by assigning work, establishing priorities, training and developing employees, monitoring work quality and safety, and collaborating with clubhouse operations and other departments within the City of Fort Collins. Essential Duties and Responsibilities • Directs and participates in daily golf course maintenance operations, establishing priorities and adapting work to weather, turf conditions, course use, staffing, and operational needs. • Plans and implements turfgrass and agronomic practices to maintain healthy turf and consistent playing conditions, including irrigation, fertility, cultural practices, and pest management. • Supervises and leads assigned maintenance staff by assigning work, establishing priorities, training employees, monitoring performance and safety, and supporting employee development. • Coordinates irrigation operations and maintenance to support efficient water use and reliable course conditions, including monitoring system performance, troubleshooting and repairs. • Coordinates the maintenance and repair of golf course equipment, facilities, and infrastructure to support safe, reliable, and efficient operations. • Supports sustainable golf course management and environmental stewardship practices through responsible management of water, fertilizers, pesticides, equipment, and other resources. • Coordinates maintenance projects and operational activities with clubhouse operations, other City departments, contractors, and external partners, and responds to customer and community concerns related to golf course maintenance. • Applies City policies, safety requirements, environmental regulations, and established maintenance standards to daily operations; identifies and addresses operational concerns and escalates issues requiring higher-level direction. • Supports emergency, weather-related, and seasonal operations, including snow removal and adjusted work schedules as operational needs require. • Serves in the Golf Course Superintendent's capacity during periods of absence, providing continuity of daily operations, staff direction, and operational decision-making within established policies and delegated authority. • Works a flexible schedule, including early mornings, weekends, holidays, and occasional adjusted hours based on seasonal and operational needs. This job description is a living document and may not be all-inclusive; employees are responsible for other duties as assigned.

SUMMARY: Clerical Aides perform regular and routine duties in a variety of recreation and facility programs and specialties. EXAMPLES OF ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: The below list is intended to be illustrative of the responsibilities of the position and not all encompassing. -Greets guest, accepts and processes facility passes and registrations for specific activities within the Recreator. -Enforces rules and policies with staff and guests. -Handles and processes payments and responsible for assigned funds and receipts. -Prepares the revenue and paid-out record forms daily. -Maintains work area, facilities, supplies and equipment. -Completes a variety of paperwork including daily records, logs and incident reports. -Ensures the safety of guests and program participants. -Assist with any first aid, CPR and other medical attention as needed. -Maintains communications with other staff within recreation and reports issues or concerns (i.e. RecTrac or activity issues) to supervisory staff as needed. -Provides exceptional customer service to all guests. -Attends and participates in staff meetings and trainings. -Keeps informed of all seasonal and on-going programs. -Performs other related duties as assigned.

Summary: Provides support in the areas of facility, program, and event preparation. Sets up and dismantles tables, chairs, audio visual equipment, presentation materials, and kitchen equipment in all areas of the facility. Assists clients and full-time staff as needed. In addition, performs custodial responsibilities throughout the facility as required to maintain facility appearance, service to public, and operational status. Work Schedule This position works out of Recreation facilities including Senior Center, and/or Club Tico. This position works up to 29 hours per week and hours may vary based on location, program, and event needs – flexibility in scheduling preferred. Early morning, late night, weekend, and holiday availability strongly desired. Essential Duties and Responsibilities: The following duties and responsibilities are illustrative of the primary functions of this position and are not intended to be all inclusive. · - Works independently and as a member of a collaborative team to provide exceptional activities, services, and resources to the public. · - Responsible for needs of programs, drop-in activities, and facility rentals while on duty. · - Provides custodial services throughout the facility as needed including laundry, sweeping, mopping, vacuuming, trash collection, storage organization, kitchen prep/clean-up as needed, and light snow removal between Parks Department clearing efforts. · - Sets-up and dismantles equipment throughout the facility including tables, chairs, audio visual equipment, presentation materials, and kitchen equipment. · - Conducts regular head counts, sanitizing rounds, and supply replenishment throughout the facility, and notifies supervisors of any inventory needs. · - Completes forms for task completion, safety/incident reports, and facility/equipment repairs. · - Communicates with on-site facility renters and completes pre- and post-rental survey forms. · - Supports front desk team with member check-in and answering phones as needed. · - Monitors and secures the facility as needed, including communication and enforcement of facility regulations. · - May operate 15 passenger vans for transportation of equipment with provided training. · - Completes required Department and City trainings and attends staff meetings as scheduled. Supervisory Responsibilities: This position is not responsible for the supervision of employees.

requisitions.externalDescription: Job Summary Are you passionate about making a positive impact in the Fort Collins community? Join the City of Fort Collins as a Bus Operator and enjoy a rewarding career with exceptional benefits. #INDHP Why Choose Transfort? Competitive Pay: Starting pay of $24.00 per hour! People-First Culture: At Transfort, we put our people first, creating a team-focused and welcoming environment where everyone feels appreciated. Exceptional paid training program. We offer an exceptional paid training program designed to ensure your success as a Bus Operator. Whether you're new to driving large vehicles or already have experience, our dedicated team of trainers will guide you through a fun, engaging, and hands-on program. Comprehensive Benefits: Access to medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your family, along with paid vacation, holidays, sick leave, life insurance, and more. Flexible Opportunities: We offer a range of positions to suit your needs, from hourly roles to classified positions with guaranteed hours and benefits. Engaging Work Environment: Join a team that not only works hard but also celebrates successes together. We believe in creating an environment were coming to work is a joy, not a chore. Available Positions We offer various employment options, including: Classified Positions: Guaranteed hours per week, offering full benefits. Hourly Positions: Ideal for those seeking flexibility, with variable hours based on availability and operational needs. During the interview process, we'll discuss current openings and work with you to identify the position that best aligns with your preferences and our operational needs. Note to Applicants: The next Transfort Bus Operator training class is scheduled to begin on November 23, 2026. Essential Duties and Responsibilities The following duties and responsibilities are illustrative of the primary functions of this position and are not intended to be all inclusive. Provides reliable, safe, and consistent public transportation service. Reports for work by start time and fit to perform job duties. Keeps all required licenses and certifications current and in possession while driving. Operates buses and other vehicles in accordance with Federal, State and local regulations. Operates a variety of wheelchair lifts, securement devices, bike racks and other safety-related equipment. Makes quick and safe decisions based on traffic and unexpected obstacles; practices defensive driving. Handles emergency and occasionally stressful situations appropriately. Performs required vehicle inspections and reports any defects appropriately. Complies with all traffic regulations and reports delays or accidents. Uses sound professional judgment in accordance with City of FC and Transfort Vision, Mission and Values. Operates different types of buses and other City vehicles in a wide variety of traffic, road and weather conditions. Operates a two-way radio and mobile data terminal to communicate with other drivers, dispatchers and supervisors. Treats all customers respectfully, providing information and answers to any questions. Management Responsibilities No

Summary: Group swim instructors provide group lesson instruction in swimming techniques, skills, and water safety to participants. This position also has the opportunity to additionally schedule and teach private swim lessons, but it is not required. Essential Duties and Responsibilities : The following duties and responsibilities and illustrative of the primary functions of this position and are not intended to be all-inclusive. • Educates the swimming public to the habits and attitudes of safe aquatic activities and encourages their cooperation and support with good public relations. • Leads group swim instruction for kids of various ages and skill levels classes of up to 6 participants. • Maintains a safe environment for all students. • Accurately judges placement of students for swim instruction. • Prepares and signed all aquatic certificates. • Correctly utilizes and cares for all aquatic equipment and teaching aides. • Maintains a level of physical fitness required fulfilling any rescue or emergency procedure for any circumstance. • Attends and participates in all required City sponsored clinics, workshops, and meetings. • Assists in the maintenance and care of the facility, including cleaning duties. • Performs any other related or similar duties as assigned. Supervisory Responsibilities: This position is not responsible for the supervision of employees.

Summary: Instructs aqua fitness classes at the City’s aquatic facilities. Classes vary from pre/post-natal water fitness, arthritis, generalized water fitness and deep-water fitness. Essential Duties and Responsibilities: The following duties and responsibilities and illustrative of the primary functions of this position and are not intended to be all inclusive. Instruction of safe, enjoyable aqua fitness classes. Assist in the maintenance and care of program equipment, facilities, and environment. Attend and participate in all required City sponsored trainings and meetings. Knowledge and enforcement of aquatic policies and operating procedures. Maintaining a level of physical fitness appropriate to the demands of the instructors’ position. Knowledge and ability to assist with emergency procedures regarding First Aid/CPR/AED, whistle blows, and accident and incident reports. Maintaining a current certification of an accredited national fitness or water fitness certification. Maintaining a current certification of First Aid/CPR/AED or obtain within 90 days of hire. Understanding of wellness principles, basic physiology, and safe exercise techniques, and the ability to communicate this information clearly to the participants. Maintenance of documents including attendance forms and consent forms. Communication with supervisors regarding concerns, comments, requests, complaints as necessary. Performance of related work as required. Supervisory Responsibilities: This position is not responsible for the supervision of employees.

Summary: Performs supervisory, administrative and aquatic tasks at the City’s aquatic facilities. Essential Duties and Responsibilities : The following duties and responsibilities and illustrative of the primary functions of this position and are not intended to be all inclusive. Supervises and is responsible for all programs and staff in the facility while on duty. Is liaison between guests and staff Maintains the equipment, facilities, and environment in a safe and sanitary condition. May have to maintain filter system within guidelines. Maintain proper chemical balance cleanliness of pool water and deck. Assumes responsibilities of taking disciplinary action as necessary while on duty. Reports all exceptional occurrences to the supervisor. Performs related work as required. Supervisory Responsibilities: Exercised supervision over personnel as assigned.

Summary: Performs in a lifeguard position protecting the life and well-being of each patron using the aquatic facility. Essential Duties and Responsibilities : The following duties and responsibilities and illustrative of the primary functions of this position and are not intended to be all inclusive. Prevention of any accidents by eliminating the hazard or a hazardous behavior. Enforcing all rules involving pool policy and operation procedure. Knowledge of all rules and justification for the rules. Educated the swimming public to the habits and attitudes of safe recreation and encourages their cooperation. Maintains a level of physical fitness appropriate to the demands of life guarding required to fulfill any emergency procedure for any circumstance. Assists in the maintenance and care of the equipment, facilities, and environment including cleaning duties. Attends and participates in all required City sponsored clinics, workshops, and meetings. Informs the supervisor of any disciplinary problems as necessary. Performs any other related or similar duty as assigned. Supervisory Responsibilities: This position is not responsible for the supervision of employees.

Summary: Lifeguard instructors provide instruction in the proper lifeguarding techniques, skills, and water safety to participants. Essential Duties and Responsibilities : The following duties and responsibilities and illustrative of the primary functions of this position and are not intended to be all inclusive. Educates lifeguard candidates to the habits and attitudes of safe aquatic activities and encourages their cooperation and support with good public relations. Maintains a safe environment for all students. Accurately judges lifeguard candidate’s ability to perform required skills. Prepares and submits all course records in a timely manner as required by the American Red Cross. Correctly utilizes and cares for all aquatic equipment and teaching aides. Maintains a level of physical fitness required to teach any rescue or skill as dictated by the American Red Cross. Attends and participates in all required City sponsored clinics, workshops, and meetings. Assists in the maintenance and care of the facility while teaching. Performs any other related or similar duties as assigned. Supervisory Responsibilities: This position is not responsible for the supervision of employees.
